    "sql_query": "WITH \n-- 1. Raw Data Extraction\nraw_laptop_data AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_model_id,\n        laptop_name,\n        laptop_brand,\n        office_battery_result_minutes,\n        gaming_battery_result_minutes,\n        mobility_score\n    FROM `ai-riser-505908.laplaptech_hardware.dim_laptops_obt` \n    WHERE laptop_model_id IS NOT NULL\n),\n\n-- 2. Data Cleaning & Standardization\ncleaned_laptop_data AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_model_id,\n        laptop_name,\n        laptop_brand,\n        COALESCE(office_battery_result_minutes, 0) AS office_battery_min,\n        COALESCE(gaming_battery_result_minutes, 0) AS gaming_battery_min,\n        COALESCE(mobility_score, 0) AS mobility_score,\n        -- Standardize brand names to avoid duplicates due to casing\n        UPPER(TRIM(laptop_brand)) AS brand_standardized\n    FROM raw_laptop_data\n),\n\n-- 3. Metric Calculation: Stability Index\n-- Since 'stability' isn't a direct column, we derive it from a combination of \n-- battery performance (office and gaming) and mobility score. \n-- A 'stable' machine is one that provides consistent, high performance across \n-- different usage scenarios (battery life) and is portable.\nstability_metrics AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_model_id,\n        laptop_name,\n        brand_standardized,\n        office_battery_min,\n        gaming_battery_min,\n        mobility_score,\n        -- Calculate a weighted stability score: \n        -- (Office Battery + Gaming Battery) / 2 * Mobility Score / 100 (normalized)\n        -- We use SAFE_DIVIDE to prevent division by zero errors.\n        ROUND(\n            SAFE_DIVIDE(\n                (office_battery_min + gaming_battery_min),\n                2\n            ) * SAFE_DIVIDE(mobility_score, 100),\n            2\n        ) AS stability_index\n    FROM cleaned_laptop_data\n),\n\n-- 4. Aggregation Layer: Comparing Stability across Models\n-- We rank the laptops based on the stability index to identify the 'most stable' machine.\nranked_stability AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_model_id,\n        laptop_name,\n        brand_standardized,\n        stability_index,\n        -- Use a window function to rank laptops by stability index\n        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY stability_index DESC) as stability_rank\n    FROM stability_metrics\n),\n\n-- 5. Final Presentation\nfinal_presentation AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_name AS machine_name,\n        brand_standardized AS brand,\n        stability_index,\n        stability_rank,\n        -- Create a human-readable label for stability level\n        CASE \n            WHEN stability_rank = 1 THEN 'Most Stable' \n            WHEN stability_rank <= 3 THEN 'Highly Stable' \n            ELSE 'Standard' \n        END AS stability_status\n    FROM ranked_stability\n)\n\n-- Output the final dataset sorted by stability rank for comparison\nSELECT * \nFROM final_presentation\nORDER BY \n    stability_rank ASC;",

Standardization & Cleaning: Handle NULLs and ensure data types are consistent\ncleaned_laptop_data AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_model_id, \n        laptop_name, \n        laptop_brand, \n        cpu_name, \n        gpu_name, \n        COALESCE(office_battery_result_minutes, 0) AS office_battery_min, \n        COALESCE(gaming_battery_result_minutes, 0) AS gaming_battery_min, \n        COALESCE(mobility_score, 0) AS mobility_score\n    FROM raw_laptop_data\n),\n\n-- 3. Metric Calculation: Define 'stability' based on available metrics. \n-- Since a specific 'stability_score' column doesn't exist in the schema, \n-- we assume stability is derived from the consistency of battery performance \n-- or the presence of all key hardware specs. \n-- For this subtask, we specifically look for devices where the 'mobility_score' (a proxy for stability/efficiency) is 0.\nstability_analysis AS (\n    SELECT \n        *,\n        CASE \n            WHEN mobility_score = 0 THEN 'Unstable/Missing Data' \n            ELSE 'Stable' \n        END AS stability_status\n    FROM cleaned_laptop_data\n),\n\n-- 4. Aggregation Layer: Identify devices with 0 stability/mobility score to check integrity\nintegrity_check AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_brand, \n        COUNT(1) AS total_devices_with_zero_stability,\n        -- Collect a list of laptop names to investigate specific failures\n        STRING_AGG(laptop_name, ', ') AS affected_laptops\n    FROM stability_analysis\n    WHERE stability_status = 'Unstable/Missing Data'\n    GROUP BY \n        laptop_brand\n),\n\n-- 5. Final Presentation: Format the output for the data integrity report\nfinal_presentation AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_brand,\n        total_devices_with_zero_stability,\n        affected_laptops,\n        -- Calculate the percentage of unstable devices per brand\n        ROUND(\n            SAFE_DIVIDE(\n                total_devices_with_zero_stability, \n                (SELECT COUNT(1) FROM cleaned_laptop_data)\n            ) * 100, \n            2\n        ) AS pct_of_total_fleet_unstable\n    FROM integrity_check\n)\n\nSELECT * \nFROM final_presentation\nORDER BY total_devices_with_zero_stability DESC;",

Raw Data Extraction: Retrieve necessary columns from the hardware table\nraw_hardware_data AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_model_id,\n        laptop_name,\n        laptop_brand,\n        cpu_name,\n        gpu_name,\n        office_battery_result_minutes,\n        gaming_battery_result_minutes,\n        mobility_score\n    FROM `ai-riser-505908.laplaptech_hardware.dim_laptops_obt`\n),\n\n-- 2. Data Cleaning & Standardization: Handle NULLs and ensure data types are consistent\ncleaned_hardware_data AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_model_id,\n        laptop_name,\n        laptop_brand,\n        COALESCE(cpu_name, 'Unknown CPU') AS cpu_name,\n        COALESCE(gpu_name, 'Unknown GPU') AS gpu_name,\n        COALESCE(office_battery_result_minutes, 0) AS office_battery_result_minutes,\n        COALESCE(gaming_battery_result_minutes, 0) AS gaming_battery_result_minutes,\n        COALESCE(mobility_score, 0) AS mobility_score\n    FROM raw_hardware_data\n),\n\n-- 3. Metric Calculation: Identify laptops with stability/mobility score of 0\n-- Note: The user request asks for 'stability' (ổn định), but based on the schema, \n-- 'mobility_score' is the closest proxy for stability/performance metrics in this OBT.\nstability_analysis AS (\n    SELECT \n        *,\n        CASE \n            WHEN mobility_score = 0 THEN 'Zero Score' \n            ELSE 'Positive Score' \n        END AS stability_status\n    FROM cleaned_hardware_data\n    WHERE mobility_score = 0\n),\n\n-- 4. Aggregation Layer: Analyze the distribution of zero-score laptops by Brand and CPU/GPU\n-- This helps identify if the issue is systemic to a specific hardware configuration\nroot_cause_aggregation AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_brand,\n        cpu_name,\n        gpu_name,\n        COUNT(laptop_model_id) AS count_zero_score_laptops,\n        AVG(office_battery_result_minutes) AS avg_office_battery,\n        AVG(gaming_battery_result_minutes) AS avg_gaming_battery\n    FROM stability_analysis\n    GROUP BY \n        laptop_brand,\n        cpu_name,\n        gpu_name\n),\n\n-- 5. Final Presentation: Format and rank the potential root causes\nfinal_presentation AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_brand AS brand,\n        cpu_name AS cpu,\n        gpu_name AS gpu,\n        count_zero_score_laptops AS total_affected_models,\n        ROUND(avg_office_battery, 2) AS avg_office_battery_min,\n        ROUND(avg_gaming_battery, 2) AS avg_gaming_battery_min,\n        -- Identify if the zero score is likely due to missing battery data\n        CASE \n            WHEN avg_office_battery = 0 AND avg_gaming_battery = 0 THEN 'Missing Battery Data' \n            ELSE 'Calculation Error or Low Performance' \n        END AS suspected_root_cause\n    FROM root_cause_aggregation\n)\n\nSELECT * \nFROM final_presentation\nORDER BY total_affected_models DESC;",

    "sql_query": "WITH \n-- 1. Raw Data Extraction: Retrieve laptop hardware and battery data\nraw_battery_data AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_model_id,\n        laptop_name,\n        laptop_brand,\n        cpu_name,\n        gpu_name,\n        office_battery_result_minutes,\n        gaming_battery_result_minutes,\n        mobility_score\n    FROM `ai-riser-505908.laplaptech_hardware.dim_laptops_obt`\n),\n\n-- 2. Standardization & Cleaning: Identify missing values and handle NULLs\ncleaned_battery_data AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_model_id,\n        LOWER(TRIM(laptop_name)) AS laptop_name,\n        LOWER(TRIM(laptop_brand)) AS laptop_brand,\n        LOWER(TRIM(cpu_name)) AS cpu_name,\n        LOWER(TRIM(gpu_name)) AS gpu_name,\n        COALESCE(office_battery_result_minutes, 0) AS office_battery_min,\n        COALESCE(gaming_battery_result_minutes, 0) AS gaming_battery_min,\n        COALESCE(mobility_score, 0) AS mobility_score,\n        -- Flagging missing data for analysis\n        CASE WHEN office_battery_result_minutes IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_office_battery_missing,\n        CASE WHEN gaming_battery_result_minutes IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_gaming_battery_missing\n    FROM raw_battery_data\n),\n\n-- 3. Aggregation Layer: Analyze missing data patterns by Brand and CPU\nmissing_data_analysis AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_brand,\n        cpu_name,\n        COUNT(laptop_model_id) AS total_models,\n        SUM(is_office_battery_missing) AS missing_office_count,\n        SUM(is_gaming_battery_missing) AS missing_gaming_count,\n        -- Calculate the percentage of missing data per group\n        ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(is_office_battery_missing), COUNT(laptop_model_id)) * 100, 2) AS office_missing_pct,\n        ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(is_gaming_battery_missing), COUNT(laptop_model_id)) * 100, 2) AS gaming_missing_pct\n    FROM cleaned_battery_data\n    GROUP BY \n        laptop_brand,\n        cpu_name\n),\n\n-- 4. Final Presentation: Format and rank the causes of missing data\nfinal_presentation AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_brand,\n        cpu_name,\n        total_models,\n        missing_office_count,\n        missing_gaming_count,\n        office_missing_pct,\n        gaming_missing_pct,\n        -- Identify the severity of the data gap\n        CASE \n            WHEN office_missing_pct > 50 OR gaming_missing_pct > 50 THEN 'Critical Gap'\n            WHEN office_missing_pct > 20 OR gaming_missing_pct > 20 THEN 'Moderate Gap'\n            ELSE 'Low Gap'\n        END AS data_gap_severity\n    FROM missing_data_analysis\n)\n\nSELECT * \nFROM final_presentation\nORDER BY \n    office_missing_pct DESC, \n    gaming_missing_pct DESC;",

Raw Data Extraction & Hard Filtering\nraw_laptop_data AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_model_id, \n        laptop_name, \n        laptop_brand, \n        cpu_name, \n        gpu_name, \n        office_battery_result_minutes, \n        gaming_battery_result_minutes, \n        mobility_score\n    FROM `ai-riser-505908.laplaptech_hardware.dim_laptops_obt` \n    WHERE laptop_model_id IS NOT NULL\n),\n\n-- 2. Data Cleaning & Standardization\ncleaned_laptop_data AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_model_id, \n        laptop_name, \n        COALESCE(laptop_brand, 'Unknown') AS laptop_brand, \n        cpu_name, \n        gpu_name, \n        COALESCE(office_battery_result_minutes, 0) AS office_battery_result_minutes, \n        COALESCE(gaming_battery_result_minutes, 0) AS gaming_battery_result_minutes, \n        COALESCE(mobility_score, 0) AS mobility_score\n    FROM raw_laptop_data\n),\n\n-- 3. Stability Metric Calculation\n-- Since the schema provided does not contain explicit 'uptime', 'error rate', or 'latency' columns,\n-- we must derive a 'stability' proxy based on the available hardware benchmarks (battery life and mobility score).\n-- In a real-world scenario, these would be found in a fct_device_logs or fct_system_metrics table.\n-- Given the current schema, we define stability as a combination of high battery efficiency and high mobility score.\nstability_scoring AS (\n    SELECT \n        *,\n        -- Normalize and score stability based on battery and mobility\n        -- Higher battery life and mobility score generally correlate with better hardware stability/efficiency\n        (office_battery_result_minutes + gaming_battery_result_minutes + (mobility_score * 10)) AS stability_index\n    FROM cleaned_laptop_data\n),\n\n-- 4. Identify the Top 1 Most Stable Machine\ntop_stable_machine AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_model_id, \n        laptop_name, \n        laptop_brand, \n        cpu_name, \n        gpu_name, \n        office_battery_result_minutes, \n        gaming_battery_result_minutes, \n        mobility_score, \n        stability_index\n    FROM stability_scoring\n    ORDER BY stability_index DESC\n    LIMIT 1\n),\n\n-- 5. Final Presentation\nfinal_presentation AS (\n    SELECT \n        laptop_name AS machine_name, \n        laptop_brand AS brand, \n        cpu_name AS processor, \n        gpu_name AS graphics_card, \n        -- We present the battery results as proxies for operational stability (uptime/efficiency)\n        office_battery_result_minutes AS office_uptime_minutes, \n        gaming_battery_result_minutes AS gaming_uptime_minutes, \n        mobility_score AS stability_score, \n        -- Calculate a percentage of total battery life relative to the average of all machines\n        ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(stability_index, (SELECT AVG(stability_index) FROM stability_scoring)), 2) AS stability_relative_to_avg\n    FROM top_stable_machine\n)\n\nSELECT * \nFROM final_presentation;",
